item.title: [Itrfoundation] Iowa’s November Election Highlights the Importance of Voter Turnout on Local Issues
item.description:
Iowa’s move to November bond elections has increased voter participation, but some local measures still draw relatively few voters. Iowa broke its midterm voter turnout record, with preliminary reports showing more than 1.38 million ballots cast, representing 63.4% of registered voters. The statewide constitutional amendment received slightly less participation, with turnout of 56%. While statewide races receive much of the attention, voters also decided important local issues. Two counties voted on the size of their boards of supervisors, nearly 50 bond proposals appeared on local ballots, and communities considered questions involving township governance, library boards, emergency medical services (EMS) taxes, local option sales taxes, and hotel and motel taxes.

item.title: [Pioneerinstitute] Florida’s evolving public education system needs fact-based discussion
item.description:
The state’s education market isn’t the problem. It just needs the right design. I have tremendous respect for Pinellas County School Board member Laura Hine’s commitment to public service, her passion for serving our community’s children and her desire to improve Florida’s public education system. But her recent column, “Is unregulated capitalism the best way to educate Florida kids?,” frames the issue too starkly. Florida’s education system is changing rapidly, and the questions surrounding these changes are too nuanced and consequential to be reduced to a choice between traditional public education and “unregulated capitalism.”

The post Florida’s evolving public education system needs fact-based discussion appeared first on Pioneer Institute.
